intro: Ambedkar's public voice ran from the Bombay Legislative Council to the Round Table Conferences, the Constituent Assembly, the Rajya Sabha and finally the Deekshabhoomi ground. Dates and venues are from Writings and Speeches (BAWS) and the Constituent Assembly Debates.

items.title: Mahad Satyagraha address
items.quote: It is not as if drinking the water of the Chavdar tank will make us immortal. We are going to the tank to assert that we too are human beings like others.
items.context: Spoken to the delegates before the march to the Chavdar tank. The December 1927 conference, with its burning of the Manusmriti, is sometimes compared by him to the French National Assembly of 1789.

items.title: Plenary address, First Round Table Conference
items.quote: The Depressed Classes... are not anxious that the British Government should go. But they do not want to be left to the mercies of a Government which would be a Government of the castes.
items.context: He told the Conference the Depressed Classes had gained nothing from a century of British rule and wanted a government 'of the people, by the people and for the people', with safeguards.

items.title: Yeola Conversion Conference
items.quote: Though I was born a Hindu, I solemnly assure you that I will not die a Hindu.
items.context: Announced after five years of failed temple-entry satyagraha. Twenty-one years later he fulfilled the vow at Nagpur.
items.source: Keer, Dr. Ambedkar: Life and Mission

items.title: Annihilation of Caste (undelivered)
items.quote: Caste is not a physical object like a wall of bricks or a line of barbed wire... Caste is a notion; it is a state of the mind.
items.context: Printed at his own expense after the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal withdrew its invitation.

items.title: Address to the Depressed Classes Women's Conference
items.quote: I measure the progress of a community by the degree of progress which women have achieved.
items.context: Delivered during the founding session of the Scheduled Castes Federation. He urged the women not to marry their children young, to treat husbands as friends and equals, and to refuse to be 'slaves'.

items.title: Ranade, Gandhi and Jinnah
items.quote: Hero-worship in the sense of the worship of a hero or a great man, which involves surrender of will, judgment and reason, is a source of great mischief.
items.context: The 101st birthday address on Justice M.G. Ranade.

items.title: Introducing the Draft Constitution
items.quote: The Draft Constitution has sought to forge means and methods whereby India will have federation and at the same time will have uniformity in all basic matters which are essential to maintain the unity of the country.
items.context: He defended the choice of a parliamentary over a presidential system, the strong Centre, the Directive Principles and the retention of the village as a unit only in administration, not in the Constitution: 'What is the village but a sink of localism, a den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism?'

items.title: Article 32: 'the heart and soul of the Constitution'
items.quote: If I was asked to name any particular Article in this Constitution as the most important... I could not refer to any other Article except this one. It is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.
items.context: On the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of fundamental rights.

items.title: Closing speech: 'The Grammar of Anarchy'
items.quote: On the 26th of January 1950, we are going to enter into a life of contradictions. In politics we will have equality and in social and economic life we will have inequality... How long shall we continue to live this life of contradictions?
items.context: He urged abandoning satyagraha and civil disobedience now that constitutional methods existed, warned against laying liberties at the feet of a great man, and said political democracy cannot last unless it rests on social democracy.

items.title: Statement on resignation from the Cabinet
items.quote: To leave inequality between class and class, between sex and sex, which is the soul of Hindu society, untouched and to go on passing legislation relating to economic problems is to make a farce of our Constitution and to build a palace on a dung heap.
items.context: Read out after he was refused permission to make a personal statement in the House.

items.title: BBC interview (film)
items.quote: Democracy in India is only a top-dressing on an Indian soil which is essentially undemocratic.
items.context: The best-known moving-picture record of Ambedkar speaking, in which he discusses the future of democracy in India and his plan to convert to Buddhism.

items.title: Why I like Buddhism
items.quote: I prefer Buddhism because it gives three principles in combination, which no other religion does. Buddhism teaches prajna (understanding as against superstition and supernaturalism), karuna (love) and samata (equality). This is what man wants for a good and happy life.
items.context: Broadcast for Buddha Jayanti in the 2500th year of the Buddhist era.

items.title: Speech after the Dhamma Diksha
items.quote: I am starting this movement of conversion at a time when, I believe, I can lead it to success... This conversion has given me enormous satisfaction and pleasure unimaginable. I feel as if I have been liberated from hell.
items.context: A two-hour speech in Marathi explaining why Nagpur, why Buddhism, and why his followers must now live as Buddhists and not as a new caste.

items.title: Buddha or Karl Marx
items.quote: The Buddha's method was different. His method was to change the mind of man: to alter his disposition: so that whatever man does, he does it voluntarily without the use of force or compulsion.
items.context: His last public lecture, sixteen days before his death.
